findings.description: The new release procedure's exact command, `git push origin main --follow-tags`, is blocked by the unmodified git-safety hook, contradicting this PR's central premise that the fix now allows it.
findings.body:
This PR's whole premise — stated in [`docs/design/0001-architecture.md` decision 26](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/c1224a0b67e81cc179a2d31bf533ac48f3c3a2fe/docs/design/0001-architecture.md#L580-L599) and [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/c1224a0b67e81cc179a2d31bf533ac48f3c3a2fe/CHANGELOG.md#L13-L15) — is that "the git-safety policy no longer blocks pushing a release tag from the trunk." This section then instructs, verbatim:

```bash
npm version patch
git push origin main --follow-tags
```

But [`templates/agents/hooks/policies/git-safety.sh`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/c1224a0b67e81cc179a2d31bf533ac48f3c3a2fe/templates/agents/hooks/policies/git-safety.sh#L44-L66) — unchanged by this PR — has **two** separate trunk-push guards. The first (L58-62) correctly exempts a tag push via `is_tag_push()`. The second, unconditional guard (L64-66):
```bash
if printf '%s' "$COMMAND" | grep -qE "git[[:space:]]+push[[:space:]]+.*[[:space:]]$TRUNK([[:space:]]|$)"; then
  block "direct push to $TRUNK. Open a pull request instead."
fi
```
has no `is_tag_push` exemption at all, and its regex matches `git push origin main --follow-tags` (`.* ` = `origin`, then a space, then `main`, then the trailing space before `--follow-tags`). Verified both by static trace and by executing the script directly against this exact command: it exits 2 with `BLOCKED by agentspine git-safety: direct push to main. Open a pull request instead.`

A maintainer following this section verbatim will be blocked. The underlying fix decision 26 describes and attributes to "decision 22" (itself a misattribution — decision 22 is about skill-invocation keys, unrelated to git-safety) only patched the first guard; the second was never updated to share the exemption.

findings.description: The new "Cutting a release" section instructs `npm version patch` (which commits and tags) directly on the trunk, contradicting AGENTS.md's unqualified "Never commit to `main`. Branch per change, PRs only." with no documented exception.
findings.body:
[AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/c1224a0b67e81cc179a2d31bf533ac48f3c3a2fe/AGENTS.md) states under "## Git workflow": **"Never commit to `main`. Branch per change, PRs only."** — unconditional, with no release-time carve-out anywhere in the document.

This PR's new ["Cutting a release" section](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/c1224a0b67e81cc179a2d31bf533ac48f3c3a2fe/CONTRIBUTING.md#L78-L85) reads:
```
From the trunk, once the change is merged:

npm version patch        # minor / major as the change warrants
git push origin main --follow-tags
```
`npm version patch` bumps `package.json` and, by default (no `.npmrc` or lifecycle override in this repo changes this), creates a git **commit** and tag on whatever branch is checked out — here, explicitly "the trunk." That is a commit landing on `main` outside a branch/PR, exactly what AGENTS.md forbids. Nothing in AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md carves out an exception for releases, and the git-safety hook's own agent-tooling scope doesn't change what the written rule says for a human following this doc.

findings.description: release.yml re-types ci.yml's entire gate-step list verbatim with no shared source or drift-check, unlike this project's own established precedent for the identical two-artifacts-must-agree problem.
findings.body:
[`release.yml` L48-61](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/c1224a0b67e81cc179a2d31bf533ac48f3c3a2fe/.github/workflows/release.yml#L48-L61) re-types [`ci.yml`'s gate commands](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/c1224a0b67e81cc179a2d31bf533ac48f3c3a2fe/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L16-L41) character-for-character: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, the full `node dist/cli.js --check ...` invocation, the full `shellcheck -s bash ...` glob list, `./scripts/audit-templates.sh`, `./scripts/audit-authors.sh`, `./scripts/verify-package.sh`. There is no `workflow_call`, no composite action, and no test asserting the two lists match. `release.yml`'s own header comment asserts "Every gate from ci.yml runs again here" — a guarantee enforced only by whoever remembers to update both files. If a future PR adds a gate to `ci.yml` and forgets `release.yml`, both stay green and that guarantee silently becomes false at exactly the moment (a tag push, possibly against a commit CI never saw, per the same comment) it matters most.

This project already has a checked safeguard for the identical problem shape elsewhere: `scripts/render-review-workflow.mjs` (a generator) paired with `test/workflow-sync.test.ts`, which fails CI if the committed `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml` drifts from what the generator renders. `release.yml`/`ci.yml` reintroduce the same "two pipeline definitions must stay identical" shape without that safeguard, and nothing in this PR's ADR entry or CHANGELOG records that omission as an accepted tradeoff.

findings.description: package.json was bumped to 0.1.1 but package-lock.json was left at 0.1.0; claude-code-review.yml's bare `npm ci` (no fallback, unlike ci.yml/release.yml) will fail on the next run against main.
findings.body:
This PR bumps [`package.json`'s version to `0.1.1`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/c1224a0b67e81cc179a2d31bf533ac48f3c3a2fe/package.json#L3) but does not touch `package-lock.json`, whose root `version` (and `packages[""].version`) is still `0.1.0`.

`.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml` has a "Build review tooling from the base branch" step, present in both the PR-review job and the comment-triggered job ([L108-119](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/c1224a0b67e81cc179a2d31bf533ac48f3c3a2fe/.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml#L108-L119) and [L296-310](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agentspine/blob/c1224a0b67e81cc179a2d31bf533ac48f3c3a2fe/.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml#L296-L310)), that runs a bare `npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix "$dir"` against a fresh worktree of `origin/<base>` — with **no** `|| npm install` fallback, unlike `ci.yml` and `release.yml` which both use `npm ci || npm install`.

`npm ci`'s own sync-check (`lib/utils/validate-lockfile.js` in npm's source) walks the full inventory including the root package entry, and throws `Invalid: lock file's agentspine@0.1.0 does not satisfy agentspine@0.1.1` on exactly this mismatch. Once this PR merges, the next PR or `@claude review` comment that triggers `claude-code-review.yml` will hit this failure before the reviewer tooling can even build, breaking the dogfooded review workflow itself.
findings.suggestion: Run `npm install` to regenerate `package-lock.json` at 0.1.1 and commit it alongside the `package.json` bump in this PR.

findings.description: "Decision 21's header also claimed..." is an imprecise citation — the quoted phrase lived in the workflow file's header comment (and render-review-workflow.mjs's HEADER constant), not in decision 21's own ADR text, which only references that file.

No tag-protection ruleset restricts who can push a `v*` tag or requires it point at a commit that passed CI; anyone with repo write access can trigger a publish. By design (release.yml re-runs every gate), but worth a ruleset if tightening is ever desired.
`npm install -g npm@latest` floats to whatever npm resolves at tag-push time rather than pinning a specific version, adding one moving supply-chain input to the publish job.
`npm ci || npm install` falls back to a potentially different dependency resolution if the lockfile is out of sync — a pattern already present in ci.yml, not introduced by this PR.

package.json's `prepublishOnly` script reruns build+test a second time inside `npm publish`, redundant with release.yml's explicit earlier build/test steps — harmless but adds a few minutes per release.

process_issues.description: This run's .claude-pr/ snapshot only contained .claude/ and CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md/.agents/templates as the claude-code-review.yml workflow comment (RESTORE_PATHS="AGENTS.md .agents templates") says it should copy there. Did not block the review — gh pr diff / git diff against the merge base gave the real PR content for those paths regardless — but the .claude-pr/ snapshot mechanism itself appears incomplete in this run.
